overview: The committee reviewed various revenue sources for the FY25 budget, including Chapter 70 state aid and revolving funds, and received an update on the current fiscal year's financial status. The administration presented a plan for a revenue collection audit and proposed a new methodology for charging administrative overhead to self-sustaining programs.

items.title: FY24 Budget Deficit Update
items.summary: Finance Director Gerry McCue reported that a previously projected $2.5 million deficit for the current year has been reduced to approximately $250,000 through the identification of new grant resources and the correction of a formula error in the projections.

items.title: Chapter 70 State Aid Projections
items.summary: The district anticipates a $135,000 increase in Chapter 70 funding for FY25 under the governor's budget, receiving minimum per-pupil aid despite a slight enrollment decline.

items.title: Revolving Funds and Program Deficits
items.summary: The committee examined balances in vocational, athletic, and rental accounts, noting specific concerns regarding operating deficits in the public pool and community schools programs.

items.title: Revenue Collection Audit and Rate Setting
items.summary: Members requested a comprehensive rate card for all tuition-based programs and rentals for FY25 approval. The administration announced an upcoming management review by an auditing firm to centralize and tighten revenue collection practices.

items.title: Private Grants and Social Responsibility Funds
items.summary: The finance director reviewed private donations and grants, including the Cummings Foundation grant that supports the Center for Citizenship and Social Responsibility.

items.title: Administrative and Facility Chargeback Proposal
items.summary: The administration proposed a methodology to recover facility and administrative costs from programs like the after-school program by charging fees based on classroom usage and employee counts.
